terms.definition: Magnetomotive force: the number of turns in a coil times the current in amperes. Rearrange to solve for current or turns.

equations.plain: Magnetomotive force is turns times current.
Rearranged: current is force over turns, and turns is force over current.
Worked from the source: 3 turns at 12 A make 36 ampere-turns.
Worked from the source: 5 turns at 4 A make 20 ampere-turns.
Worked from the source: 18 ampere-turns on 6 turns takes 3 A.
Worked from the source: 32 ampere-turns at 8 A takes 4 turns.
Worked from the source: 7 turns at 9 A make 63 ampere-turns.
Worked from the source: 45 ampere-turns on 9 turns takes 5 A.
Ampere-turns, written out: turns times current.
Problem 1, substituted: 3 turns times 12 A.
Problem 1, answered: 36 ampere-turns.
Problem 2, substituted: 5 turns times 4 A.
Problem 2, answered: 20 ampere-turns.
Problem 3, substituted: 18 ampere-turns equals 6 turns times the unknown current.
Problem 3, solved for current: 18 divided by 6.
Problem 3, answered: 3 A.
Problem 4, substituted: 32 ampere-turns equals the unknown turns times 8 A.
Problem 4, solved for turns: 32 divided by 8.
Problem 4, answered: 4 turns.
Problem 5, substituted: 7 turns times 9 A.
Problem 5, answered: 63 ampere-turns.
Problem 6, substituted: 45 ampere-turns equals 9 turns times the unknown current.
Problem 6, solved for current: 45 divided by 9.
Problem 6, answered: 5 A.

terms.definition: The NEC article for radio and television receiving equipment, antenna masts, lead-in conductors, grounding, bonding, and satellite receiving systems.

The loss of optical signal power along a fiber span, written as an attenuation coefficient in dB/km — about 0.35 dB/km at 1310 nm and 0.20 dB/km at 1550 nm. A 20 km run at 1310 nm loses 7 dB in the fiber alone, before any connector or splice losses.

symbols.label: P(L)
symbols.meaning: optical power at distance L from the source (linear units, e.g. mW)

symbols.label: P0
symbols.meaning: launch power at the source (linear units, e.g. mW)

symbols.label: dB
symbols.meaning: decibels — here, the loss in the fiber alone

equations.plain: Power falls off exponentially with distance: every kilometer multiplies it by the same fraction, set by α.
In decibels the same loss is a subtraction: received power is launch power minus α times the length.
Worked from the source: 20 km at 0.35 dB/km costs 7 dB of fiber loss.

terms.definition: The four maximally entangled two-qubit states, which form an orthonormal basis for two-qubit systems. Applying H then CNOT to |00⟩ produces the first of them.

symbols.label: |Φ<sup>±</sup>⟩
symbols.meaning: the two Bell states built from |00⟩ and |11⟩

symbols.label: |Ψ<sup>±</sup>⟩
symbols.meaning: the two Bell states built from |01⟩ and |10⟩
two-qubit basis states: both qubits 0; both qubits 1
two-qubit basis states with the qubits different
plus or minus: one sign gives each state of the pair

equations.plain: The first Bell state is an equal blend of both-zero and both-one — measure one qubit and you know the other.
All four Bell states: equal blends of matching (Φ) or opposite (Ψ) qubit values, with a plus or minus sign.

terms.definition: Protects one logical qubit against a single bit-flip error by encoding it across three physical qubits. Measuring the stabilizers Z₁Z₂ and Z₂Z₃ (parity checks) detects and corrects an error on any one of the three without collapsing the logical state.

equations.plain: Logical 0 is stored as three physical zeros, logical 1 as three ones.

terms.definition: Any pure qubit state written in spherical coordinates: the polar angle sets the mix of |0⟩ and |1⟩, the azimuthal angle the relative phase. The north pole is |0⟩, the south pole is |1⟩, and the equator is maximum superposition.

symbols.meaning: the basis state 0 (a ket: a state vector)

symbols.label: θ
symbols.meaning: polar angle, from 0 to π: the mix of |0⟩ and |1⟩

symbols.label: φ
symbols.meaning: azimuthal angle, from 0 to 2π: the relative phase

symbols.label: e
symbols.meaning: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm (≈ 2.718)

equations.plain: Any pure qubit state is a point on a sphere, fixed by two angles.
At θ = 0 the state sits at the north pole: |0⟩.
At θ = π the state sits at the south pole: |1⟩.

terms.definition: A capacitor's opposition to AC current flow, in ohms. It decreases as frequency increases; with a capacitive load, current leads voltage.

symbols.label: Xc
symbols.meaning: capacitive reactance (ohms, Ω) — lowercase c, as written in the source notes

symbols.label: f
symbols.meaning: frequency of the AC signal (hertz, Hz)

equations.plain: Reactance is one over 2π times frequency times capacitance — so it falls as frequency rises.
The same relationship, as written in the theory section.
The same relationship, as written in the study notes.

terms.definition: Splitters in series — for example a 1:4 feeding four 1:8s, which gives an effective 1:32 split. Their losses add cumulatively.

symbols.label: ILcascade
symbols.meaning: total insertion loss of the cascade (dB)

symbols.label: IL1, IL2
symbols.meaning: insertion loss of the first and second splitter stage (dB)

symbols.label: N1, N2
symbols.meaning: split ratio of the first and second stage

symbols.label: dB (ideal)
symbols.meaning: decibels, ideal — excess loss not included

equations.plain: Two splitters in a row lose the sum of their losses, each set by its own split ratio.
Worked from the source: a 1:4 (6.0 dB) feeding a 1:8 (9.0 dB) loses 15.0 dB ideal — the same as one 1:32.

terms.definition: The NEC article for community antenna television and radio distribution systems — coaxial CATV or radio distribution.
The NEC article for Class 1 power-limited, remote-control, and signaling circuits.
The NEC article for Class 2 and Class 3 power-limited circuits — control, signaling, and low-voltage control wiring.
The NEC article for Class 4 fault-managed power systems.
The fundamental two-qubit entangling gate: it flips the target qubit when the control qubit is 1. Applying H then CNOT to |00⟩ produces a Bell state.

symbols.label: CNOT
symbols.meaning: the controlled-NOT gate, a 4×4 matrix acting on two qubits

equations.plain: CNOT leaves |00⟩ and |01⟩ alone and swaps |10⟩ with |11⟩.

terms.definition: Cable with a copper core and shielding, carrying electrical signals.
The NEC article for communications wiring from the service point to terminal equipment: cable types, building pathways, listing, separation, and installation methods for voice and data circuits.

The NEC article for scope and definitions shared across communications systems; grounding and bonding; equipment and cable listing; protection at the building entrance; cable installation and separation; and references that apply across the later Chapter 8 articles. When a rule is common to several communications technologies, start here.

Signal loss per unit length in copper cable, which generally increases with frequency. In the simplified model, the √f term models conductor (skin-effect) loss and the f term models dielectric loss; the constants depend on the cable's construction and materials.

symbols.label: α
symbols.meaning: attenuation: signal loss per unit length (dB/m or dB/ft)

symbols.label: f
symbols.meaning: frequency of the transmitted signal (hertz, Hz)

symbols.label: k1, k2
symbols.meaning: constants set by the cable's construction and materials

equations.plain: Copper loss climbs with frequency: a square-root part from the skin effect plus a straight-line part from the dielectric.
The same model, as written in the study notes.

terms.definition: The angle at the core–cladding boundary beyond which light is totally internally reflected back into the core. It is set by the refractive indices of the core and the cladding.

symbols.label: θ<sub>c</sub>
symbols.meaning: critical angle at the core–cladding boundary (degrees)

symbols.label: arcsin
symbols.meaning: inverse sine: the angle whose sine is the value given

equations.plain: The critical angle is the angle whose sine is the cladding's index divided by the core's index.

terms.definition: A power ratio on a logarithmic scale. Doubling power is approximately +3 dB, halving it approximately −3 dB, and multiplying it by ten is +10 dB.

symbols.label: ΔPdB
symbols.meaning: change in power, in decibels (dB) — as written in the study notes

equations.plain: A change in dB is ten times the base-10 log of the power ratio.
The same definition, as written in the theory section.
Twice the power is about 3.01 dB more.
Worked from the study notes: doubling the power gives 10 × log₁₀(2) ≈ 3.01 dB.

terms.definition: The loss of a qubit's quantum state through interaction with its environment.
Carrying many wavelengths of light on one fiber at once. A single single-mode strand with DWDM can carry more than 100 Tbps in laboratory conditions.
Determines in a single query whether a function f:{0,1}→{0,1} is constant or balanced — something that requires two queries classically. The function is encoded as an oracle gate.

symbols.label: Uf
symbols.meaning: the oracle: a gate that encodes f

symbols.label: |x⟩, |y⟩
symbols.meaning: the input qubit and the output qubit

equations.plain: The oracle leaves the input alone and XORs f of the input into the output qubit.
Constant: f gives the same output for both inputs.
Balanced: f gives different outputs for the two inputs.

terms.definition: The rate at which a circuit delivers energy, in watts. With any two of voltage, current, and resistance known, the identities give the power.

equations.plain: Power is voltage times current — or current squared times resistance, or voltage squared over resistance.
The same identities, as written in the theory section.
Worked from the source: 4 A through 12 Ω dissipates 192 W.
Worked from the source: 240 V across 60 Ω dissipates 960 W.
Worked from the source: a 48 V circuit supplying 2.5 A delivers 120 W.
Worked from the study notes: 4 A through 12 Ω, via current squared, is 192 W.
Worked from the study notes: 240 V across 60 Ω, via voltage squared, is 960 W.
Power is voltage times current.
Worked from the study notes: 48 V times 2.5 A is 120 W.

terms.definition: Once two qubits are entangled, measuring one instantly determines the state of the other, regardless of physical separation. This is not faster-than-light signalling: no classical information is transmitted.
Cable that transmits data as pulses of light through ultra-pure glass or plastic strands — light through glass, where copper carries electricity through metal.

How close an actual, possibly mixed, state is to the ideal state. F = 1 is a perfect qubit; F = 0.5 is completely mixed (classical). Error correction requires fidelity above the fault-tolerance threshold (~99.0–99.9% depending on the code).

symbols.label: ⟨ψ|
symbols.meaning: the bra: the conjugate transpose of |ψ⟩

symbols.label: ρ
symbols.meaning: the actual, possibly mixed, state (a density matrix)

equations.plain: Fidelity measures how much of the ideal state survives in the actual one.
F = 1: a perfect qubit.
F = 0.5: completely mixed — no better than classical.

terms.definition: The NEC article for circuit-integrity, fire-resistive cable — cable that must survive fire exposure.
A gigabit passive optical network. Upstream and downstream travel on separate wavelengths — 1310 nm upstream, 1490 nm downstream.
Searches an unsorted database of N items in O(√N) queries where classical search needs O(N) — a quadratic speedup: about 2³² steps instead of 2⁶⁴ for 2⁶⁴ entries.

symbols.label: k
symbols.meaning: the optimal number of Grover iterations before measuring

symbols.label: n
symbols.meaning: the number of qubits in the register
floor: round down to a whole number

equations.plain: Run about π/4 times the square root of N iterations, rounded down, then measure.
An n-qubit register holds 2 to the n items.

terms.definition: A single-qubit gate that creates an equal superposition from a basis state.

symbols.meaning: the basis state 0 (a ket: a state vector)
the plus and minus states: equal superpositions with a + or − sign

equations.plain: The Hadamard matrix: all entries ±1, scaled by one over root two.
Hadamard turns |0⟩ into the plus state and |1⟩ into the minus state.

terms.definition: For an ideal transformer, voltage follows the turns ratio, current varies inversely with turns, and apparent input power equals apparent output power.

symbols.label: Np, Ns
symbols.meaning: number of turns in the primary and secondary winding

equations.plain: Voltage ratio equals turns ratio.
Current ratio is the turns ratio flipped.
Secondary voltage is the primary voltage scaled by the turns ratio.
Worked from the source: 240 V on a 200:50 transformer gives 60 V.
Secondary current is the primary current scaled by the inverted turns ratio.
Worked from the source: 5 A on a 600:150 transformer gives 20 A.
Power in equals power out: primary volts times amps equal secondary volts times amps.
Worked from the source: 120 V at 8 A in, 480 V out, means 2 A out.
Worked from the study notes: 240 V times 50/200 is 60 V.
Worked from the study notes: power balance solved for secondary current — 120 × 8 ÷ 480 = 2 A.
equations.tex: V_p \times I_p = V_s \times I_s \implies I_s = \frac{V_p \times I_p}{V_s} = \frac{120 \times 8}{480} = \frac{960}{480} = 2\text{ A}

equations.plain: Worked from the study notes: 5 A times 600/150 is 20 A.

terms.definition: An inductor's opposition to AC current flow, in ohms. It increases as frequency increases; with an inductive load, current lags voltage.

symbols.label: f
symbols.meaning: frequency of the AC signal (hertz, Hz)

equations.plain: Reactance is 2π times frequency times inductance — so it climbs as frequency rises.
The same relationship, as written in the study notes.

terms.definition: Delay DSL adds on top of propagation delay — up to 20 ms on ADSL2+.
The sum of currents entering a node equals the sum leaving it.

symbols.label: I1, I2
symbols.meaning: current in each parallel branch (amperes, A)

symbols.label: Itotal
symbols.meaning: total current entering or leaving the parallel circuit (A)

symbols.label: Itotal
symbols.meaning: total current entering or leaving the parallel circuit (A) — as written in the study notes

equations.plain: Worked from the source: at 120 V, a 40 Ω branch draws 3 A and a 60 Ω branch 2 A.
By KCL the source supplies the branches' sum: 5 A.
The same branch currents, as written in the study notes.
The same total, as written in the study notes: 3 + 2 = 5 A.

terms.definition: The algebraic sum of voltage rises and drops around a closed loop is zero — the voltage drops around any loop add up to the source voltage.
Fiber with a numerical aperture of about 0.20–0.50: a wider acceptance cone, used over shorter distances.
The NEC article for network-powered broadband communications systems — broadband powered from the network side.

A load that does not draw current in proportion to the applied sinusoidal voltage. Its distorted current is a fundamental plus harmonic components; electronic power supplies and rectifier-input loads commonly produce them. Harmonics add current distortion and heating in conductors and transformers, and triplen harmonics in four-wire wye systems can add in the neutral rather than cancel.

symbols.label: i(t)
symbols.meaning: the instantaneous current at time t (amperes, A)

symbols.label: ω
symbols.meaning: angular frequency of the fundamental (radians per second)

symbols.label: φ1, φn
symbols.meaning: phase angle of the fundamental and of the nth harmonic (radians)

symbols.label: Σn=2∞
symbols.meaning: sum over the harmonics n = 2, 3, 4, … without end

equations.plain: Distorted current is the fundamental sine wave plus a stack of harmonics at whole-number multiples of its frequency.

terms.definition: A measure of the cone of light a fiber accepts, set by the core and cladding refractive indices. Single-mode fiber: NA ≈ 0.12 — a tight beam, one propagation mode, minimal dispersion. Multimode fiber: NA ≈ 0.20–0.50.

equations.plain: The acceptance of a fiber is the square root of the difference between the squared core and cladding indices.

terms.definition: The relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in a circuit.

equations.plain: Voltage equals current times resistance.

terms.definition: The NEC article for optical fiber cables and raceways: fiber backbone, transmission by light.
A small device installed at the customer's premises that converts the optical signal to Ethernet; the customer's router connects to the ONT's Ethernet port.
What the link can afford to lose: transmitter power minus the receiver's minimum. The full end-to-end loss from OLT to ONT must stay within it.

symbols.label: Ltotal
symbols.meaning: total end-to-end loss, OLT to ONT (dB)

symbols.label: Σ ILsplit
symbols.meaning: the sum of every splitter's insertion loss (dB)

symbols.label: M
symbols.meaning: system margin for ageing and temperature (dB)

symbols.label: fiber · splitters · connectors · splices · margin
symbols.meaning: the labels under the braces, naming each term

equations.plain: The budget is what the transmitter puts out minus the least the receiver can still read.
Total loss is fiber, splitters, connectors, and splices added up — with the system margin carried as one more line item.

terms.definition: A network that uses passive 1:N optical splitters. Each split divides the optical power equally — but the loss in dB does not divide equally: it adds logarithmically.
The bit flip, or quantum NOT.

equations.plain: Pauli-X swaps the two basis states: |0⟩ becomes |1⟩ and back.

terms.definition: Single-qubit gates that leave |0⟩ alone and shift the phase of |1⟩.

symbols.label: e
symbols.meaning: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm (≈ 2.718)

equations.plain: S multiplies the |1⟩ part by i (a quarter turn); T by e to the iπ/4 (an eighth turn).

terms.definition: Lattice-based and hash-based algorithms resistant to Shor's algorithm; standardized by NIST in 2024.

A ratio between 0.0 and 1.0 relating real power to apparent power. A purely resistive AC load has a power factor of 1.0. Where waveform distortion is present, distinguish displacement power factor from true power factor.
Apparent power (VA), real power (W), and reactive power (VAR) relate like the sides of a right triangle, so reactive power follows from the other two.

symbols.label: S
symbols.meaning: apparent power: the total delivered to the circuit (volt-amperes, VA)

symbols.label: P
symbols.meaning: real (active) power: the power doing work (watts, W)

equations.plain: Reactive power is the square root of apparent power squared minus real power squared.
Apparent power squared equals real power squared plus reactive power squared.
Worked from the source: 10,000 VA and 8,000 W leave 6,000 VAR.
Worked from the study notes, every step shown: 6,000 VAR.

terms.definition: The NEC article for cables for power-limited circuits and fault-managed power circuits — a generic power-limited or fault-managed power cable without a class number.
The NEC article for premises-powered broadband communications systems — customer-side powered optical network equipment.
The time a signal takes to cross a span. Light travels through silica fiber at about 2 × 10⁸ m/s — roughly two-thirds of its speed in vacuum — so a 100 km span adds about 0.5 ms one way.

The quantum analogue of the discrete Fourier transform and the core subroutine of Shor's algorithm and quantum phase estimation. It runs in O(n²) gates on an n-qubit register, where the classical FFT runs in O(N log N).

symbols.label: N
symbols.meaning: the number of basis states (N = 2ⁿ for n qubits)

symbols.label: Σk=0N−1
symbols.meaning: sum over k from 0 to N − 1

symbols.label: x, k
symbols.meaning: integer labels of the input and output basis states

symbols.label: e
symbols.meaning: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm (≈ 2.718)

equations.plain: The QFT spreads one input state over every output state, each with a phase that turns with x times k.

terms.definition: A unitary transformation of qubit states. All quantum gates are unitary matrices.

equations.plain: Undoing a gate is always possible: U-dagger times U gives back the identity.

terms.definition: Quantum algorithms exploit constructive interference to amplify correct answers and destructive interference to cancel wrong ones.
Key exchange such as the BB84 protocol, in which eavesdropping disturbs the quantum state and so becomes detectable. Commercial deployments exist.
A quantum bit. A classical bit is always 0 or 1; a qubit exists in a superposition of both, weighted by complex probability amplitudes. Measurement collapses the superposition irreversibly.

symbols.meaning: the basis state 0 (a ket: a state vector)

equations.plain: A qubit's state is a weighted blend of 0 and 1.
The two probabilities must add up to one.

terms.definition: For a sinusoidal waveform, the effective AC voltage: the peak voltage divided by √2, about 0.707 of the peak.

symbols.label: Vrms
symbols.meaning: root-mean-square voltage: the effective AC voltage (volts, V)

symbols.label: Vpeak
symbols.meaning: peak voltage: the maximum amplitude of the waveform (V)

symbols.label: Vrms
symbols.meaning: root-mean-square voltage (V) — as written in the study notes

symbols.label: Vpeak
symbols.meaning: peak voltage (V) — as written in the study notes

equations.plain: RMS is peak over root two — about 0.707 of the peak.
RMS is 0.707 of the peak.
Worked from the source: a 170 V peak is about 120 V RMS.
Worked from the study notes: 170 V peak times 0.707 is about 120 V.

terms.definition: Resistances in series add directly.

symbols.label: Rtotal
symbols.meaning: total resistance of the series circuit (ohms, Ω)

symbols.label: Rtotal
symbols.meaning: total resistance of the series circuit (Ω) — as written in the study notes

equations.plain: Total series resistance is the sum of the parts.
Worked from the source: 10 + 15 + 25 = 50 Ω.
Worked from the study notes: 10 + 15 + 25 = 50 Ω.

terms.definition: The maximum theoretical throughput of a channel, set by its bandwidth and its signal-to-noise ratio. Fiber's near-zero noise floor and multi-THz optical bandwidth give it a theoretical capacity orders of magnitude above copper.

equations.plain: Capacity grows in step with bandwidth, but only with the logarithm of the signal-to-noise ratio.

terms.definition: A quantum error-correcting code that uses 9 physical qubits per logical qubit and corrects arbitrary single-qubit errors (X, Z, and Y).
Fiber with a 9 µm core that carries a single light mode with virtually no modal dispersion, enabling multi-gigabit speeds over distances exceeding 40 km without amplification.

The loss a passive 1:N optical splitter puts on each output. The ideal (theoretical) loss is set by the split ratio alone; real splitters add excess loss from manufacturing imperfections — typically 0.1–0.5 dB for a PLC splitter.

symbols.label: ILsplit
symbols.meaning: ideal splitting loss of a 1:N splitter (dB)

symbols.label: ILactual
symbols.meaning: actual insertion loss, excess loss included (dB)

symbols.label: N
symbols.meaning: split ratio: the number of outputs

equations.plain: Splitting light N ways costs ten times the base-10 logarithm of N, in dB — 3 dB for every halving.
A real splitter loses the ideal amount plus its excess loss.

terms.definition: The real power of a balanced three-phase load, from line-to-line voltage, line current, and power factor. √3 (≈ 1.732) is the line-to-line multiplier for three-phase systems.

symbols.label: PF
symbols.meaning: power factor, between 0.0 and 1.0 — as written in the study notes

equations.plain: Three-phase power is root three times voltage times current times power factor.
Worked from the source: 480 V, 10 A, PF 1.0 gives about 8,314 W.
Worked from the study notes: 1.732 × 480 × 10 × 1.0 ≈ 8,314 W.

terms.definition: When light strikes the core–cladding boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle, it reflects entirely back into the core with zero energy lost to the cladding — the fundamental mechanism that makes fiber work.
Copper wire pairs over which traditional telco infrastructure (DSL, POTS) transmits electrical signals.
